techniques.name: Interior-point method (Barrier method)
techniques.capability_it_enables: polynomial-time constrained convex optimization
techniques.summary_verbatim: IPM-LSTM proposes using LSTM neural networks to approximate the solution of linear systems within an interior point method, reducing iterations by up to 60% and solution time by up to 70%.
mechanism_atoms: A logarithmic barrier function is added to the objective, penalizing proximity to constraint boundaries and transforming the constrained problem into an unconstrained one
The barrier parameter is decreased iteratively along the central path, a curve of optimal solutions parameterized by the barrier weight
Newton's method is applied at each barrier value to solve the perturbed KKT conditions, giving a search direction
Primal and dual variables are updated simultaneously via a predictor-corrector step to track the central path
Convergence is certified when the duality gap (complementarity measure) falls below a specified tolerance

techniques.name: ADMM (Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers)
techniques.capability_it_enables: decomposable distributed convex optimization with consensus constraints
techniques.summary_verbatim: ADMM is a popular first-order method owing to its simplicity and efficiency.
mechanism_atoms: The augmented Lagrangian L_rho(x,z,y) = f(x) + g(z) + y^T(Ax+Bz-c) + (rho/2)||Ax+Bz-c||^2 is formed by dualizing the coupling constraint
The x-update minimizes L_rho over x with z and y fixed (primal block minimization)
The z-update minimizes L_rho over z with x and y fixed (primal block minimization, often solved by the proximal operator of g)
The dual variable y is updated by a gradient ascent step: y <- y + rho*(Ax+Bz-c)
Iterating these three steps converges to a primal-dual solution pair for linearly constrained convex problems

techniques.name: Proximal gradient method
techniques.capability_it_enables: efficient minimization of smooth+nonsmooth composite objectives (e.g., lasso, group sparsity)
techniques.summary_verbatim: A splitting algorithm for the minimization of the sum of two convex functions, one of which is smooth, with applications in mechanics, inverse problems, machine learning, image reconstruction, and statistics.
mechanism_atoms: The objective is split into a smooth differentiable part f and a (possibly nonsmooth) regularizer g
A gradient step on f is taken: x_half = x_k - alpha * grad f(x_k)
The proximal operator prox_{alpha*g}(x_half) = argmin_z { g(z) + (1/2alpha)||z - x_half||^2 } is then applied
Nesterov momentum (FISTA) can be added by maintaining an extrapolation point, improving convergence from O(1/k) to O(1/k^2)
The step size alpha must satisfy alpha < 1/L where L is the Lipschitz constant of grad f

techniques.name: Natural gradient descent
techniques.capability_it_enables: parameter-invariant steepest descent on statistical manifolds for neural network training
techniques.summary_verbatim: Natural gradient descent uses the gradient times the inverse of the model's Fisher information matrix in place of the standard gradient.
mechanism_atoms: The Fisher information matrix F(theta) = E[grad log p(x|theta) grad log p(x|theta)^T] defines the Riemannian metric on the statistical manifold
The natural gradient is g_nat = F(theta)^{-1} * grad L, replacing the Euclidean gradient with a curvature-corrected direction
This makes the update invariant to reparameterization of the model, unlike ordinary gradient descent
In practice, K-FAC and other block-diagonal approximations make the F^{-1} computation tractable for large networks
The update follows the steepest descent direction under the KL divergence metric between distributions

techniques.name: Frank-Wolfe (Conditional Gradient) method
techniques.capability_it_enables: projection-free constrained optimization yielding sparse iterates
techniques.summary_verbatim: The purpose of this survey is to serve both as a gentle introduction and a coherent overview of state-of-the-art Frank--Wolfe algorithms, also called conditional gradient algorithms, for function minimization.
mechanism_atoms: At each iteration, a linear approximation of the objective is minimized over the feasible set: s_k = argmin_{s in C} <grad f(x_k), s>
The iterate is updated by a convex combination: x_{k+1} = (1-gamma)*x_k + gamma*s_k, where gamma in [0,1] is a step size
No projection onto the constraint set is needed, making it cheaper than projected gradient when the linear subproblem is easy
Iterates are naturally sparse convex combinations of extreme points of the feasible set
Convergence rate is O(1/k) for smooth convex objectives; variants achieve linear convergence under strong convexity

techniques.name: Variational inference (ELBO optimization)
techniques.capability_it_enables: scalable approximate Bayesian posterior inference via optimization
techniques.summary_verbatim: Variational inference (VI) is a leading approximate inference method in which a posterior distribution p(z|x) is approximated by a simpler distribution q(z) from some approximating family.
mechanism_atoms: The Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) = E_q[log p(x,z)] - E_q[log q(z)] is derived from Jensen's inequality applied to log p(x)
Maximizing the ELBO is equivalent to minimizing the KL divergence KL(q(z) || p(z|x)) between the variational and true posterior
In mean-field VI, q(z) = prod_i q_i(z_i) is assumed; each factor is updated by coordinate ascent: log q_j(z_j) = E_{-j}[log p(x,z)] + const
Stochastic variants (SVI, ADVI) use mini-batches and reparameterization gradients to scale to large data
The gap between ELBO and log p(x) quantifies the approximation error; tighter bounds reduce this gap

techniques.name: Importance sampling
techniques.capability_it_enables: low-variance Monte Carlo estimation by reweighting samples from a proposal distribution
techniques.summary_verbatim: Importance sampling is a popular variance reduction method for Monte Carlo estimation, where a notorious question is how to design good proposal distributions.
mechanism_atoms: The target expectation E_p[f(x)] is rewritten as E_q[f(x)*w(x)] where w(x) = p(x)/q(x) is the importance weight
Samples x_1,...,x_n are drawn from the proposal distribution q rather than the target p
The IS estimator (1/n) sum_i f(x_i)*w(x_i) is unbiased when q has support covering p
Self-normalized IS divides by the sum of weights to handle the case when the normalizing constant of p is unknown
Variance is minimized when q is proportional to |f(x)|*p(x); in practice, adaptive methods learn better proposals

techniques.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC)
techniques.capability_it_enables: efficient high-dimensional Bayesian posterior sampling via gradient-guided proposals
techniques.summary_verbatim: HMC sampling methods provide a mechanism for defining distant proposals with high acceptance probabilities in a Metropolis-Hastings framework, enabling more efficient exploration of the state space than standard random-walk proposals.
mechanism_atoms: Auxiliary momentum variables p ~ N(0,M) are introduced, extending the target to a joint Hamiltonian H(q,p) = -log pi(q) + (1/2)p^T M^{-1} p
Hamilton's equations dq/dt = M^{-1}p, dp/dt = -grad_q H are simulated using the leapfrog integrator for L steps with step size epsilon
The leapfrog proposal is accepted/rejected via a Metropolis correction that exactly corrects for discretization error
Hamiltonian dynamics are time-reversible and volume-preserving (symplectic), ensuring the detailed balance condition
Stochastic Gradient HMC injects friction and noise terms to use mini-batch gradients without a Metropolis step

techniques.name: Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm
techniques.capability_it_enables: maximum-likelihood estimation in latent variable models
techniques.summary_verbatim: Expectation maximization (EM) is a technique for estimating maximum-likelihood parameters of a latent variable model given observed data by alternating between taking expectations of sufficient statistics, and maximizing the expected log likelihood.
mechanism_atoms: E-step: compute the expected complete-data log-likelihood Q(theta|theta_old) = E_{Z|X,theta_old}[log p(X,Z|theta)] using the current parameters
M-step: maximize Q over theta to obtain the new parameter estimate: theta_new = argmax_theta Q(theta|theta_old)
Each EM iteration is guaranteed to be monotonically non-decreasing in log p(X|theta)
Convergence is to a stationary point (local maximum or saddle) of the observed-data likelihood
Applicable to Gaussian mixtures, HMMs, PCA, topic models; online/stochastic EM variants handle streaming data

techniques.name: Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD)
techniques.capability_it_enables: scalable Bayesian posterior sampling and non-convex optimization via noisy gradient iterations
techniques.summary_verbatim: The Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) are popularly used to approximate Bayesian posterior distributions in statistical learning procedures with large-scale data.
mechanism_atoms: SGLD updates parameters as theta_{t+1} = theta_t + epsilon_t * grad log p(theta_t|X_batch) + sqrt(2*epsilon_t) * eta_t, where eta_t ~ N(0,I)
The injected Gaussian noise of magnitude sqrt(2*epsilon_t) converts gradient descent into a discretization of the Langevin SDE
With step size epsilon_t -> 0 at the right rate, the Markov chain converges to the true posterior without a Metropolis step
Mini-batch gradient estimates enable use on large datasets at the cost of introducing a second noise source from subsampling
Two error sources arise: Euler-Maruyama discretization error and subsampling error; both are bounded in the Wasserstein metric

techniques.name: Information bottleneck method
techniques.capability_it_enables: principled dimensionality reduction preserving task-relevant information (rate-distortion with learned distortion)
techniques.summary_verbatim: This constrained optimization problem can be seen as a generalization of rate distortion theory, yielding self-consistent equations for the coding rules, with solutions found by a convergent re-estimation method that generalizes the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm.
mechanism_atoms: The goal is to find a compressed representation T of input X that preserves maximum information about label Y
The IB Lagrangian is L = I(X;T) - beta*I(T;Y), where beta trades compression against relevance
Self-consistent equations for the optimal encoder p(t|x) are derived and solved by iterative Blahut-Arimoto updates
The IB curve traces the Pareto frontier of the I(X;T) vs I(T;Y) tradeoff across all beta values
In deep learning, each layer is interpreted as a bottleneck compressing input while retaining label information

techniques.name: Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle
techniques.capability_it_enables: model selection and regularization via data compression theory
techniques.summary_verbatim: This is an up-to-date introduction to and overview of the Minimum Description Length (MDL) Principle, a theory of inductive inference that can be applied to general problems in statistics, machine learning and pattern recognition.
mechanism_atoms: MDL selects the model M that minimizes the total description length L(M) + L(data|M), trading model complexity for goodness-of-fit
L(M) encodes the model (prior), and L(data|M) encodes the data given the model using the model's code (likelihood term)
The two-part (crude) MDL uses separate codes for model parameters and prediction residuals
Refined MDL uses the Normalized Maximum Likelihood (NML) or Bayesian mixture code, which jointly encodes all data efficiently
Minimizing total codelength is equivalent to maximizing a penalized likelihood, generalizing AIC/BIC

techniques.name: Mutual Information Neural Estimation (MINE)
techniques.capability_it_enables: tractable estimation and maximization of mutual information between high-dimensional variables
techniques.summary_verbatim: Mutual information is a fundamental quantity for measuring the relationship between random variables.
mechanism_atoms: MINE uses the Donsker-Varadhan representation: I(X;Z) >= E_{p(x,z)}[T_theta(x,z)] - log E_{p(x)p(z)}[exp(T_theta(x,z))]
A neural network T_theta is trained to maximize this lower bound, providing a differentiable MI estimator
The estimator is strongly consistent and scalable to high-dimensional continuous random variables
Gradients of the MI estimate flow through T_theta, enabling joint optimization of the encoder and MI objective
Applied to GANs (mode-dropping reduction), adversarial autoencoders, and the Information Bottleneck

techniques.name: Deep InfoMax (DIM) — mutual information maximization for representations
techniques.capability_it_enables: unsupervised representation learning by maximizing input-representation mutual information
techniques.summary_verbatim: In this work, we perform unsupervised learning of representations by maximizing mutual information between an input and the output of a deep neural network encoder.
mechanism_atoms: Global DIM maximizes I(x; E(x)) between the full input x and the encoder output E(x) using a discriminator network
Local DIM additionally maximizes I(x_l; E(x)) for local patches x_l, injecting spatial structure into the objective
A Noise Contrastive Estimation (NCE)-style bound separates positive pairs (x, E(x)) from negative pairs (x', E(x))
A prior matching regularizer aligns the marginal distribution of representations to a prior via an adversarial discriminator
The representation is learned purely from unlabeled data and evaluated on downstream classification tasks

techniques.name: Variational Renormalization Group — RG / Deep Learning duality
techniques.capability_it_enables: theoretical understanding of feature hierarchy in deep networks via RG coarse-graining
techniques.summary_verbatim: We construct an exact mapping from the variational renormalization group, first introduced by Kadanoff, and deep learning architectures based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs).
mechanism_atoms: The renormalization group (RG) iteratively integrates out short-wavelength degrees of freedom to produce effective coarse-grained descriptions
Kadanoff block-spin RG on the Ising model averages spins over blocks, reducing lattice size while preserving long-range behavior
Each layer of a deep RBM realizes one RG coarse-graining step, mapping visible variables to hidden ones via learned couplings
The variational RG minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the exact and variational (RBM) distributions at each scale
Fixed points of the RG flow correspond to phase transitions; deep networks' higher layers capture increasingly global structure

techniques.name: Replica method (statistical physics for ML)
techniques.capability_it_enables: exact asymptotic characterization of learning curves and generalization in high-dimensional models
techniques.summary_verbatim: Recent years have been marked with the fast-pace diversification and increasing ubiquity of machine learning applications.
mechanism_atoms: The replica trick computes E[log Z] = lim_{n->0} (E[Z^n] - 1)/n, where n replicas of the system are introduced and the limit is taken analytically
The free energy F = -lim_{N->inf} (1/N) E[log Z] gives the typical training and test loss in the thermodynamic limit
Under replica symmetry (RS) assumption, the free energy reduces to a saddle-point equation in order parameters (overlaps between replicas)
Replica symmetry breaking (RSB) captures more complex glassy phases when RS gives non-physical solutions
This yields exact asymptotic formulas for generalization error, double-descent, and sample complexity in random feature and neural network models

techniques.name: Mean-field theory / variational inference via Wasserstein gradient flow
techniques.capability_it_enables: scalable approximate Bayesian inference with convergence guarantees via optimal transport geometry
techniques.summary_verbatim: In this work, we introduce a general computational framework to implement MF variational inference for Bayesian models, with or without latent variables, using the Wasserstein gradient flow (WGF), a modern mathematical technique for realizing a gradient flow over the space of probability measures.
mechanism_atoms: Mean-field (MF) approximation factorizes the posterior as a product of independent factors: q(z) = prod_i q_i(z_i)
Each factor q_j is updated by coordinate ascent: log q_j(z_j) = E_{-j}[log p(x,z)] + const
The Wasserstein gradient flow views MF updates as gradient descent on the KL divergence functional in the Wasserstein-2 metric space
Time-discretized WGF provides a fixed-point equation whose contraction factor bounds exponential convergence of the MF posterior
The framework handles non-conjugate models by bypassing closed-form updates via particle or numerical approximations

techniques.name: MCMC with transport map preconditioning (multifidelity MCMC)
techniques.capability_it_enables: efficient posterior sampling for expensive Bayesian inverse problems using multi-fidelity surrogates
techniques.summary_verbatim: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling of posterior distributions arising in Bayesian inverse problems is challenging when evaluations of the forward model are computationally expensive.
mechanism_atoms: A low-fidelity model is used to construct a transport map T that deterministically pushes a reference Gaussian to an approximation of the low-fidelity posterior
T defines a non-Gaussian proposal distribution q(theta') = |det DT^{-1}| * phi(T^{-1}(theta')) for the Metropolis-Hastings step
Proposals drawn from q are accepted/rejected using the high-fidelity model, guaranteeing that the stationary distribution is the true high-fidelity posterior
The transport map is learned by minimizing KL divergence between the reference distribution and the low-fidelity posterior
Multi-fidelity combination achieves significant speedup by concentrating expensive high-fidelity evaluations near the true posterior mode

techniques.name: Kalman filter
techniques.capability_it_enables: optimal linear state estimation in dynamical systems from noisy observations
techniques.summary_verbatim: State estimation is widely applied in robotics, computer vision, and time-series forecasting, aiming to estimate true system states while minimizing estimation error.
mechanism_atoms: Prediction step: x_{t|t-1} = A*x_{t-1|t-1}, P_{t|t-1} = A*P_{t-1|t-1}*A^T + Q propagates state mean and covariance through the linear dynamics
Innovation y_t = z_t - H*x_{t|t-1} is the difference between observation and predicted observation
Kalman gain K_t = P_{t|t-1}*H^T * (H*P_{t|t-1}*H^T + R)^{-1} weights the innovation optimally under Gaussian noise
Update step: x_{t|t} = x_{t|t-1} + K_t*y_t, P_{t|t} = (I - K_t*H)*P_{t|t-1} incorporates the new measurement
The filter minimizes the mean-squared estimation error and is the exact Bayesian posterior for linear-Gaussian models

techniques.name: Wavelet transform (multiscale signal decomposition)
techniques.capability_it_enables: joint time-frequency localized feature extraction for signals and images
techniques.summary_verbatim: The wavelet transform provides a powerful multiscale framework for representing signals in both the spatial and frequency domains, with strong localization properties in time and scale.
mechanism_atoms: The continuous wavelet transform CWT(a,b) = (1/sqrt(a)) integral f(t) psi*((t-b)/a) dt projects a signal onto dilated/translated mother wavelets psi
The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) uses a filter bank: a high-pass filter h and low-pass filter g decompose signals into detail and approximation coefficients at each scale
Multi-resolution analysis (MRA) produces a nested sequence of subspaces V_j such that V_j+1 = V_j + W_j, where W_j is the wavelet detail space
The fast wavelet transform runs in O(N) via iterated filter bank convolutions, compared to O(N log N) for FFT
Wavelet coefficients are sparse for piecewise-smooth signals, enabling compression and denoising via coefficient thresholding

techniques.name: Compressed sensing / sparse recovery (RIP framework)
techniques.capability_it_enables: exact reconstruction of sparse signals from far fewer measurements than the Nyquist rate
techniques.summary_verbatim: The restricted isometry property (RIP) for design matrices gives guarantees for optimal recovery in sparse linear models and is of high interest in compressed sensing and statistical learning.
mechanism_atoms: A measurement matrix Phi satisfies the RIP of order k if (1-delta)||x||^2 <= ||Phi x||^2 <= (1+delta)||x||^2 for all k-sparse vectors x
Under RIP, the underdetermined system y = Phi*x + noise has a unique k-sparse solution recoverable by solving the L1 minimization program
Basis Pursuit: min ||x||_1 subject to ||Phi x - y|| <= epsilon solves the sparse recovery problem in polynomial time via linear programming
Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) greedily selects the column of Phi most correlated with the residual at each step
Random matrices (Gaussian, Bernoulli) satisfy RIP with high probability when m = O(k log(n/k)) measurements are taken

techniques.name: Spectral clustering (graph Laplacian eigenvectors)
techniques.capability_it_enables: nonlinearly-separable clustering via spectral embedding of graph structure
techniques.summary_verbatim: Spectral clustering is a leading and popular technique in unsupervised data analysis.
mechanism_atoms: An affinity matrix W is constructed (e.g., Gaussian kernel: W_ij = exp(-||x_i - x_j||^2 / 2*sigma^2))
The graph Laplacian L = D - W (or normalized variants) is computed, where D is the degree matrix
The k smallest eigenvectors of L form a spectral embedding matrix U in R^{n x k}
Rows of U are treated as new data points and clustered by k-means in the Euclidean spectral space
The eigenvector gap determines the number of clusters; SpectralNet uses a neural network to learn the eigenmap, enabling generalization

techniques.name: Belief propagation / loopy belief propagation
techniques.capability_it_enables: approximate marginal inference and MAP estimation in graphical models via message passing
techniques.summary_verbatim: Belief propagation for general graphical models with loops provides message passing update rules and inference equations for arbitrary graphical models with loops.
mechanism_atoms: Each node i sends a message m_{i->j}(x_j) = sum_{x_i} psi_i(x_i) * phi_{ij}(x_i,x_j) * prod_{k!=j} m_{k->i}(x_i) to its neighbor j
Belief at node i is b_i(x_i) = prod_k m_{k->i}(x_i) * psi_i(x_i), giving the approximate marginal
On trees, BP is exact and converges in finite steps; on graphs with loops, it is run iteratively (loopy BP) until convergence
Loopy BP minimizes the Bethe free energy, an approximation to the true free energy of the distribution
Max-product BP (replacing sum with max) solves MAP inference; neural networks can unroll BP iterations as differentiable layers

techniques.name: PageRank (random walk stationary distribution)
techniques.capability_it_enables: node importance ranking in directed graphs; graph neural network positional encodings
techniques.summary_verbatim: The PageRank algorithm determines the ranking of each Web page by computing the stationary probability vector of a random walking process on the Web link graph.
mechanism_atoms: A random surfer model defines transition matrix P_ij = (1-d)/N + d * A_ij/out_degree(i), where d is a damping factor (~0.85)
PageRank vector pi is the stationary distribution satisfying pi = P^T * pi, solved by power iteration pi_{t+1} = P^T * pi_t
Personalized PageRank (PPR) replaces the uniform teleportation with a source-specific restart distribution
Bidirectional estimators combine forward random walks from source and reverse pushes from target to compute PPR scores in O(sqrt(m)) time
PPR vectors are used as node features in graph neural networks and for graph-based semi-supervised learning

techniques.name: Multigrid methods (hierarchical PDE solvers)
techniques.capability_it_enables: optimal O(N) solution of large sparse linear systems arising from PDE discretizations
techniques.summary_verbatim: Constructing fast numerical solvers for partial differential equations (PDEs) is crucial for many scientific disciplines, and at the core of a multigrid solver is the prolongation matrix, which relates between different scales of the problem.
mechanism_atoms: A hierarchy of grids (levels) is constructed; the finest grid has spacing h, coarser grids have spacing 2h, 4h, ...
Pre-smoothing (e.g., Gauss-Seidel) damps high-frequency error components on the fine grid
The residual r = b - A*x is restricted to the coarse grid via restriction operator R (e.g., full-weighting)
A coarse-grid correction equation A_c * e_c = R*r is solved (recursively by the same multigrid algorithm)
The correction is prolongated back to the fine grid via interpolation P and added: x <- x + P*e_c; post-smoothing removes remaining high-frequency errors

techniques.name: Krylov subspace methods / Conjugate Gradient
techniques.capability_it_enables: large-scale sparse linear system solution without forming or storing the full matrix
techniques.summary_verbatim: Krylov subspace methods are among the most efficient solvers for large scale linear algebra problems.
mechanism_atoms: The k-th Krylov subspace K_k(A, b) = span{b, Ab, A^2*b, ..., A^{k-1}*b} is built by repeated matrix-vector products
Conjugate Gradient (CG) minimizes the A-norm of the error ||x-x*||_A over K_k at each step
Orthogonal directions p_k are maintained by three-term recurrence: p_{k+1} = r_{k+1} + beta_k * p_k, eliminating the need to store all previous directions
CG converges in at most n exact steps for n x n symmetric positive-definite A; in practice, convergence depends on the condition number kappa(A)
Pipelined and communication-hiding variants restructure the recurrence to overlap global reductions with spmv operations on distributed hardware

techniques.name: Automatic differentiation (AD / autodiff)
techniques.capability_it_enables: exact efficient computation of gradients of arbitrary numerical programs via operator overloading
techniques.summary_verbatim: Derivatives, mostly in the form of gradients and Hessians, are ubiquitous in machine learning.
mechanism_atoms: Forward mode AD augments each numeric value with a derivative (dual number): (v, v') propagated through elementary operations via chain rule
Reverse mode AD (backpropagation) records a computational graph during the forward pass and then traverses it backward, accumulating gradients via the chain rule
Reverse mode computes all partial derivatives of a scalar output in one backward pass, costing O(1) times the forward computation
Forward mode is efficient when there are many outputs and few inputs; reverse mode is efficient when there are many inputs and few outputs
Higher-order derivatives and Jacobian-vector products are obtained by composing forward and reverse mode passes

techniques.name: Model Predictive Control (MPC)
techniques.capability_it_enables: real-time constrained optimal control via receding-horizon trajectory optimization
techniques.summary_verbatim: The fields of MPC and RL consider two successful control techniques for Markov decision processes and both are widely used in practical applications, including robotics, process control, energy systems, and autonomous driving.
mechanism_atoms: At each time step, MPC solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem over a prediction horizon T: min_{u_0,...,u_{T-1}} sum_t c(x_t, u_t) subject to x_{t+1} = f(x_t, u_t), constraints
Only the first control action u_0* is applied (receding horizon principle), then the horizon is shifted and re-solved at the next step
Constraints on states and inputs are enforced explicitly within the optimization, unlike unconstrained RL
Terminal cost and terminal set are added to guarantee stability of the closed-loop receding-horizon scheme
RL is used to learn the value function (terminal cost), prediction model, or to directly warm-start the MPC solver

techniques.name: Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR)
techniques.capability_it_enables: optimal feedback control for linear dynamical systems with quadratic cost; foundational for RL sample complexity analysis
techniques.summary_verbatim: This paper addresses the optimal control problem known as the Linear Quadratic Regulator in the case when the dynamics are unknown.
mechanism_atoms: The LQR minimizes J = sum_t (x_t^T Q x_t + u_t^T R u_t) for a linear system x_{t+1} = A x_t + B u_t
The optimal policy is a linear state-feedback u_t* = -K*x_t, where K = (R + B^T P B)^{-1} B^T P A
The cost matrix P satisfies the discrete-time Algebraic Riccati Equation (DARE): P = Q + A^T P A - A^T P B (R + B^T P B)^{-1} B^T P A
When A and B are unknown, system identification (SysID) learns them from rollout data; random matrix bounds control estimation error
System Level Synthesis reformulates LQR as a convex optimization over closed-loop system responses, enabling robust and learning-based variants

techniques.name: Persistent homology (topological data analysis)
techniques.capability_it_enables: multiscale topological feature extraction from data (connected components, holes, voids) robust to noise
techniques.summary_verbatim: Deeply rooted in algebraic topology, persistent homology (PH) provides a delicate balance between data simplification and intrinsic structure characterization, and has been applied to various areas successfully.
mechanism_atoms: A filtration is built by growing a simplicial complex (e.g., Vietoris-Rips) from the data as a scale parameter epsilon increases
At each epsilon, homology groups H_k track topological features: H_0 = connected components, H_1 = loops, H_2 = voids
Birth and death times of each feature are recorded as (b_i, d_i) pairs forming a persistence diagram
Persistence diagrams are compared via the Wasserstein or bottleneck distance, providing stability guarantees
Persistent homology features are vectorized (persistence images, landscapes, Betti curves) for use as inputs to ML models

techniques.name: Optimal transport (Wasserstein distance)
techniques.capability_it_enables: geometrically meaningful comparison and interpolation of probability distributions for generative modeling and domain adaptation
techniques.summary_verbatim: Recently, Optimal Transport has been proposed as a probabilistic framework in Machine Learning for comparing and manipulating probability distributions.
mechanism_atoms: The Wasserstein-p distance W_p(mu, nu) = inf_{gamma in Pi(mu,nu)} (E_{(x,y)~gamma}[d(x,y)^p])^{1/p} minimizes expected transport cost over all couplings gamma
The Kantorovich dual: W_1(mu,nu) = sup_{||f||_Lip<=1} E_mu[f] - E_nu[f] expresses W_1 as a supremum over 1-Lipschitz functions
Sinkhorn's algorithm computes a regularized OT plan (Cuturi 2013) by iteratively scaling rows and columns of the cost-exponentiated matrix
The Monge map T*: X -> Y is the deterministic optimal transport plan when it exists; flow matching and score matching learn T* via neural networks
Wasserstein GANs use the dual formulation to train a critic network as the Lipschitz function, providing stable GAN training

techniques.name: LDPC codes with neural belief propagation decoding
techniques.capability_it_enables: near-capacity error correction using learned iterative message-passing decoders
techniques.summary_verbatim: Low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes have been successfully commercialized in communication systems due to their strong error correction capabilities and simple decoding process.
mechanism_atoms: LDPC codes are defined by a sparse parity-check matrix H with few 1s per row/column, enabling efficient belief-propagation decoding
The Tanner graph has variable nodes (codeword bits) and check nodes (parity constraints); messages iterate between them
Neural BP unrolls a fixed number of BP iterations as layers of a neural network and trains weights (message-passing coefficients) end-to-end
The neural min-sum decoder learns per-edge weights to compensate for correlation in loopy graphs, improving over standard sum-product
Boosting (training two decoders in sequence) targets the error-floor region where uncorrected trapping sets cause residual errors

techniques.name: Turbo codes and deep turbo decoding
techniques.capability_it_enables: capacity-approaching error correction via iterative soft-decision decoding learnable by neural networks
techniques.summary_verbatim: We focus on Turbo codes, and propose DeepTurbo, a novel deep learning based architecture for Turbo decoding.
mechanism_atoms: Turbo codes concatenate two recursive systematic convolutional (RSC) encoders through a pseudo-random interleaver Pi
The BCJR (Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv) algorithm computes soft-output log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) for each bit using forward-backward trellis recursion
Two BCJR decoders exchange extrinsic LLR information iteratively through the interleaver/de-interleaver, converging to the joint MAP estimate
DeepTurbo replaces the structured BCJR modules with neural networks trained end-to-end without any knowledge of the BCJR algorithm
End-to-end training enables adaptation to non-AWGN channels where classical BCJR is sub-optimal

techniques.name: Mean-field approximation in graphical models (cluster variational methods)
techniques.capability_it_enables: tractable approximate inference bridging naive mean-field and exact junction-tree computation
techniques.summary_verbatim: We extend the standard mean field method by using an approximating distribution that factorises into cluster potentials.
mechanism_atoms: Cluster mean-field decomposes q(z) = prod_c q_c(z_c) over overlapping clusters c rather than individual variables
Generalized mean-field equations are derived by minimizing KL(q || p) within the cluster-factored family
Setting clusters to single variables recovers naive mean-field; setting clusters to cliques of the junction tree recovers exact inference
The method interpolates between these extremes: larger clusters give better accuracy at higher computational cost
Cluster beliefs are updated iteratively via local message computations on the approximating factor graph

techniques.name: Random walk (graph-based semi-supervised learning and embeddings)
techniques.capability_it_enables: proximity-based node representation learning, link prediction, and semi-supervised label propagation
techniques.summary_verbatim: A random walk is known as a random process which describes a path including a succession of random steps in the mathematical space.
mechanism_atoms: A random walk on graph G with transition matrix P (P_ij = W_ij / degree(i)) generates a sequence of nodes visiting the neighborhood of a source
The stationary distribution pi = P^T pi is reached in the limit; node2vec and DeepWalk sample random walks and apply skip-gram to learn embeddings
Random Walk with Restart (RWR) returns to the source node with probability (1-alpha) at each step, computing personalized PageRank
Label propagation uses random walk hitting probabilities to diffuse labels from labeled to unlabeled nodes
Graph convolutional networks implicitly perform a truncated random walk aggregation via repeated neighborhood averaging

techniques.name: Optimal transport maps for generative modeling
techniques.capability_it_enables: deterministic sample generation by directly learning the transport map between noise and data distributions
techniques.summary_verbatim: With the discovery of Wasserstein GANs, Optimal Transport (OT) has become a powerful tool for large-scale generative modeling tasks.
mechanism_atoms: The Monge problem seeks a map T: X -> Y minimizing E[c(x, T(x))] over all measure-preserving maps T pushing mu to nu
The optimal map T* is the gradient of a convex potential phi: T*(x) = grad phi(x) (Brenier's theorem for squared-Euclidean cost)
A neural network parameterizes T and is trained by minimizing a Sinkhorn or GAN-based OT objective
Flow matching learns velocity fields u_t such that the ODE dx/dt = u_t(x) transports samples along the optimal geodesic
Unlike VAEs and GANs, OT-based generators provide exact sample generation without stochastic latent noise at inference time

techniques.name: Neural belief propagation for quantum error correction
techniques.capability_it_enables: improved decoding of quantum LDPC codes by training BP decoders to handle degeneracy
techniques.summary_verbatim: Belief-propagation (BP) decoders play a vital role in modern coding theory, but they are not suitable to decode quantum error-correcting codes because of a unique quantum feature called error degeneracy.
mechanism_atoms: Quantum LDPC codes use sparse parity-check matrices for X and Z stabilizers on a qubit lattice
Classical BP fails on quantum codes because degenerate errors (different Pauli sequences with the same syndrome) cause ambiguity
Neural BP unrolls T iterations of the BP algorithm, treating edge weights as trainable parameters
The loss function is modified to account for degeneracy: degenerate errors are treated as equivalent in the training objective
Training substantially reduces the logical error rate compared to plain BP across all tested code families

techniques.name: Stochastic Replica method for ML stability
techniques.capability_it_enables: self-consistent parameter optimization and stability analysis for ensemble-based classifiers
techniques.summary_verbatim: The paper introduces a statistical physics inspired supervised machine learning algorithm for classification and regression problems.
mechanism_atoms: The method generates multiple replicas of a linear model by expanding training data in different random function bases
Voting across replicas combines predictions: f(x) = sign(sum_r w_r * F_r(x)) where F_r are outputs of different basis expansions
Invariances (stability) of predictions under perturbation of the function basis provide a signal for self-consistent parameter optimization
Parameters are tuned by maximizing agreement (overlap) between replicas on training data, analogous to the replica overlap order parameter in spin glasses
The method uses only one or two hyperparameters that are automatically determined by the stability criterion

techniques.name: Stochastic ADMM (non-convex non-smooth)
techniques.capability_it_enables: large-scale non-convex non-smooth optimization with linear constraints via stochastic splitting
techniques.summary_verbatim: ADMM is a popular first-order method owing to its simplicity and efficiency and is widely used to solve large-scale linearly constrained optimization problems, convex or nonconvex.
mechanism_atoms: The objective f(x) + g(z) with constraint Ax + Bz = c is split into independently solvable x and z subproblems
Stochastic ADMM replaces the full gradient of f with a mini-batch stochastic gradient estimate at each iteration
An augmented Lagrangian penalty rho*||Ax+Bz-c||^2/2 enforces the coupling constraint and regularizes the subproblems
Convergence to an epsilon-stationary point is proved with O(1/sqrt(K)) rate for the non-convex case under mild variance conditions
Proximal updates on g (the nonsmooth term) are solved exactly using the prox operator, decoupling the two blocks

techniques.name: FlashAttention
techniques.capability_it_enables: exact attention on long sequences without quadratic memory growth
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce the number of memory reads/writes between GPU high bandwidth memory (HBM) and GPU on-chip SRAM.
mechanism_atoms: Tiles the Q, K, V matrices into blocks that fit in on-chip SRAM to avoid full HBM materialisation
Computes softmax and attention output block-by-block using online softmax renormalisation
Requires fewer HBM accesses than standard attention by fusing all attention operations into a single CUDA kernel
Avoids storing the full N×N attention matrix, giving O(N) memory instead of O(N²)

techniques.name: FlashAttention-2
techniques.capability_it_enables: near-theoretical-peak GPU utilisation for attention computation
techniques.summary_verbatim: We present FlashAttention-2, with better parallelism and work partitioning to address these challenges.
mechanism_atoms: Reduces non-matrix-multiply FLOPs by tweaking the attention algorithm loop order
Parallelises attention computation across sequence length dimension as well as batch/head dimensions to increase GPU occupancy
Distributes work between warps on each thread block to reduce shared-memory communication overhead
Achieves ~2× speedup over FlashAttention (v1) and reaches 50–73% of theoretical peak FLOPs/s on A100

techniques.name: Grouped Query Attention (GQA)
techniques.capability_it_enables: multi-head quality with near multi-query inference speed
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a recipe for uptraining existing multi-head language model checkpoints into models with MQA using 5% of original pre-training compute, and introduce grouped-query attention (GQA), a generalization of multi-query attention which uses an intermediate (more than one, less than number of query heads) number of key-value heads.
mechanism_atoms: Partitions query heads into G groups, each group sharing a single key-value head pair
Reduces KV-cache memory footprint by factor of (H/G) where H is total query heads
Existing MHA checkpoints can be uptraining to GQA by mean-pooling key/value heads within each group at low additional compute cost
G=1 recovers Multi-Query Attention; G=H recovers Multi-Head Attention

techniques.name: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
techniques.capability_it_enables: length-extrapolatable relative positional encoding for transformers
techniques.summary_verbatim: The proposed RoPE encodes the absolute position with a rotation matrix and meanwhile incorporates the explicit relative position dependency in self-attention formulation.
mechanism_atoms: Multiplies query and key vectors by a rotation matrix whose angle is a function of absolute token position
The inner product of rotated query and key depends only on their relative position, enabling relative-position awareness without explicit relative encodings
Inter-token dependency decays naturally with increasing distance
Compatible with linear self-attention and arbitrary sequence lengths at inference time

techniques.name: ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases)
techniques.capability_it_enables: inference-time sequence length extrapolation beyond training length
techniques.summary_verbatim: ALiBi does not add positional embeddings to word embeddings; instead, it biases query-key attention scores with a penalty that is proportional to their distance.
mechanism_atoms: Adds a fixed, head-specific negative scalar times token-distance as a bias to each query-key dot product before softmax
No learned positional parameters; bias slopes are fixed per head using a geometric sequence
Induces recency bias that allows extrapolation to sequences longer than seen during training
Achieves same perplexity as sinusoidal embeddings trained on 2× longer sequences while being 11% faster and using 11% less memory

techniques.name: Sparse Attention (Longformer)
techniques.capability_it_enables: linear-scaling self-attention for documents of thousands of tokens
techniques.summary_verbatim: Longformer's attention mechanism is a drop-in replacement for the standard self-attention and combines a local windowed attention with a task motivated global attention.
mechanism_atoms: Each token attends only to a local sliding window of w neighbouring tokens (windowed attention)
Selected task-specific tokens (e.g. [CLS]) attend globally to all positions and all positions attend to them
Combines local and global patterns via dilated windows for coarser long-range context
Total complexity is O(N) instead of O(N²) in sequence length

techniques.name: Ring Attention
techniques.capability_it_enables: near-infinite context training distributed across multiple devices
techniques.summary_verbatim: We present a novel approach, Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers (Ring Attention), which leverages blockwise computation of self-attention and feedforward to distribute long sequences across multiple devices while fully overlapping the communication of key-value blocks with the computation of blockwise attention.
mechanism_atoms: Partitions the sequence across devices; each device holds one block of queries and initially one block of KV
Devices compute local attention scores while simultaneously sending their KV block to the next device in a ring topology
Communication of KV blocks is fully overlapped with compute, hiding inter-device latency
Enables sequence lengths up to (device count × single-device limit) without any approximation

techniques.name: Mamba (Selective State Space Model)
techniques.capability_it_enables: sub-quadratic sequence modeling with content-dependent state transitions
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a new class of selective state space models, in which the SSM parameters are functions of the input, addressing the weakness in prior SSMs to perform content-based reasoning.
mechanism_atoms: Extends structured SSMs (S4) by making the state-space parameters B, C, and Δ input-dependent (selective)
Selective mechanism gates which information flows into the recurrent state based on current input content
Uses a hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm for efficient GPU training despite the data-dependent parameterisation
No attention or MLP blocks; the entire architecture is a stack of selective SSM layers with an end-to-end design
Achieves linear O(N) compute and constant O(1) per-step memory during inference

techniques.name: S4 (Structured State Space Sequences)
techniques.capability_it_enables: efficient modeling of extremely long-range dependencies (up to 16k tokens)
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose the Structured State Space sequence model (S4) based on a new parameterization for the SSM, which can be computed much more efficiently.
mechanism_atoms: Parameterises the SSM's state matrix A with a low-rank correction around a diagonal plus low-rank (DPLR) structure
DPLR structure allows the SSM convolution kernel to be computed as a Cauchy matrix product, solvable in O(N log N)
Initialises A using the HiPPO framework for optimal polynomial projection of history
Can operate in either recurrent mode (O(1) per step inference) or convolutional mode (parallel training)
Achieves state-of-the-art on Long Range Arena and solves the Path-X task (length 16k) that all prior methods fail

techniques.name: Transformer (Attention Is All You Need)
techniques.capability_it_enables: parallelisable sequence transduction without recurrence
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
mechanism_atoms: Uses scaled dot-product attention: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V for each head
Multi-head attention projects Q, K, V into h subspaces, computes attention in parallel, then concatenates
Encoder-decoder structure with cross-attention allowing decoder to attend to encoder representations
Sinusoidal positional encodings injected into embeddings to supply sequence order
Layer normalisation and residual connections stabilise training

techniques.name: Switch Transformer
techniques.capability_it_enables: trillion-parameter scale training with constant per-token compute
techniques.summary_verbatim: We simplify the MoE routing algorithm and design intuitive improved models with reduced communication and computational costs.
mechanism_atoms: Each token is routed to exactly one expert (top-1 routing), simplifying the MoE gating to a single argmax
A capacity factor limits the number of tokens each expert processes per batch to prevent load imbalance
An auxiliary load-balancing loss encourages uniform token distribution across experts
Expert parallelism distributes expert FFN layers across devices, each device holding a subset of experts

techniques.name: DeepSeekMoE
techniques.capability_it_enables: higher expert specialisation by fine-grained and shared expert segmentation
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose the DeepSeekMoE architecture towards ultimate expert specialization, involving two principal strategies: finely segmenting the experts into mN ones and activating mK from them, and isolating K_s experts as shared ones.
mechanism_atoms: Fine-grained expert segmentation splits each expert FFN into m smaller sub-experts, expanding the combinatorial space of expert mixtures
Activates mK fine-grained experts per token while using the same total compute as a standard top-K MoE
Isolates a small set of shared experts that are always activated to capture common knowledge and reduce redundancy in routed experts
Routed experts can then specialise in more distinct, non-overlapping knowledge

techniques.name: Adam Optimizer
techniques.capability_it_enables: adaptive per-parameter learning rates for large-scale stochastic optimisation
techniques.summary_verbatim: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments.
mechanism_atoms: Maintains exponential moving averages of the gradient (first moment m_t) and its squared value (second moment v_t)
Applies bias-correction to m_t and v_t to compensate for their initialisation at zero
Updates parameters by dividing the bias-corrected first moment by the square root of the bias-corrected second moment plus epsilon
Requires only first-order gradients and has O(d) memory overhead for d parameters

techniques.name: AdamW (Decoupled Weight Decay)
techniques.capability_it_enables: correct L2 regularisation for adaptive gradient optimisers
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a simple modification to recover the original formulation of weight decay regularization by decoupling the weight decay from the optimization steps taken w.r.t. the loss function.
mechanism_atoms: Standard Adam applies L2 regularisation by adding λθ to the gradient before adaptive scaling, but this conflates L2 with weight decay
AdamW directly subtracts λθ from parameters after the adaptive gradient step, truly decoupling regularisation from gradient-based updates
Decoupling makes the effect of weight decay independent of gradient magnitude and learning rate
Results in substantially improved generalisation over Adam, especially with cosine annealing schedules

techniques.name: Sophia Optimizer
techniques.capability_it_enables: 2× faster LLM pre-training by incorporating diagonal Hessian curvature
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose Sophia, Second-order Clipped Stochastic Optimization, a simple scalable second-order optimizer that uses a light-weight estimate of the diagonal Hessian as the pre-conditioner.
mechanism_atoms: Estimates the diagonal Hessian every k iterations using either a Gauss-Newton approximation or Hutchinson's estimator
Divides the gradient moving average by the Hessian diagonal estimate to obtain a curvature-adapted update
Applies element-wise clipping to bound the worst-case step size and handle non-convexity
Hessian estimation adds negligible per-step memory and compute overhead since it is computed infrequently

techniques.name: Muon Optimizer
techniques.capability_it_enables: ~2× training compute efficiency improvement over AdamW for LLMs
techniques.summary_verbatim: Muon internally runs standard SGD-momentum, and then performs an orthogonalization post-processing step, in which each 2D parameter's update is replaced with the nearest orthogonal matrix.
mechanism_atoms: Computes Nesterov-style momentum gradient update for each matrix parameter
Applies Newton-Schulz iteration (5 steps) to orthogonalise the update matrix, replacing it with the nearest orthogonal matrix
Newton-Schulz iteration runs stably on GPU tensor cores: X ← aX + bX(X^TX) iterated until convergence
Orthogonal updates preserve spectral norm and update all singular values equally
Weight decay and per-parameter scale calibration are added to stabilise large-scale LLM training

techniques.name: Shampoo
techniques.capability_it_enables: efficient approximate full-matrix preconditioning for tensor parameters
techniques.summary_verbatim: Shampoo maintains a set of preconditioning matrices, each of which operates on a single dimension, contracting over the remaining dimensions.
mechanism_atoms: For a weight matrix W ∈ R^(m×n), maintains left preconditioner L ∈ R^(m×m) and right preconditioner R ∈ R^(n×n)
Updates L ← L + G G^T and R ← R + G^T G using gradient G each step
Applies the update W ← W - η L^{-1/4} G R^{-1/4} using matrix pth-roots computed periodically
Reduces preconditioning compute from O(m³n³) to O(m³ + n³) by exploiting Kronecker factorisation

techniques.name: Batch Normalisation
techniques.capability_it_enables: stable training of very deep networks with high learning rates
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a new mechanism, which we call Batch Normalization, that takes a step towards reducing internal covariate shift, and in doing so dramatically accelerates the training of deep neural nets.
mechanism_atoms: Normalises each feature dimension to zero mean and unit variance using statistics computed over the mini-batch
Applies learnable scale (γ) and shift (β) parameters to restore representational capacity after normalisation
At inference, uses running statistics (exponential moving averages of batch mean and variance) rather than batch statistics
Inserted before or after non-linearities in convolutional or fully-connected layers

techniques.name: Layer Normalisation
techniques.capability_it_enables: normalisation invariant to batch size, applicable to RNNs and Transformers
techniques.summary_verbatim: Unlike batch normalization, layer normalization performs exactly the same computation at training and test times.
mechanism_atoms: Computes mean and variance across all features within a single sample (not across the batch dimension)
Normalises each sample's feature vector to zero mean and unit variance independently
Applies learnable affine parameters γ and β after normalisation
Per-sample computation makes it independent of batch size and applicable to sequential/recurrent architectures

techniques.name: RMSNorm
techniques.capability_it_enables: faster normalisation than LayerNorm with comparable accuracy
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose root mean square layer normalization (RMSNorm), which regularizes the summed inputs to a neuron in one layer with the root mean square (RMS) statistic alone.
mechanism_atoms: Normalises activations by dividing by their root mean square: RMS(x) = sqrt(mean(x²))
Omits the mean-centring (re-centering) step of LayerNorm, keeping only the re-scaling step
Applies a learnable scale parameter g after RMS normalisation
Reduces computation by ~7–64% vs LayerNorm because it avoids mean computation and subtraction

techniques.name: Dropout
techniques.capability_it_enables: preventing co-adaptation of neurons to reduce overfitting
techniques.summary_verbatim: The key idea is to randomly drop units (along with their connections) from the neural network during training, which prevents units from co-adapting too much.
mechanism_atoms: Each unit is retained with probability p (typically 0.5) independently at each training step
Dropped units contribute neither forward activations nor gradient updates in that step
At test time, all units are active but their weights are scaled by p to match expected training-time activations
Approximates averaging predictions over an exponential ensemble of thinned sub-networks

techniques.name: GELU Activation
techniques.capability_it_enables: smooth stochastic-gating nonlinearity outperforming ReLU on NLP/CV tasks
techniques.summary_verbatim: The GELU nonlinearity weights inputs by their value, rather than gates inputs by their sign as in ReLUs.
mechanism_atoms: Defined as GELU(x) = x · Φ(x), where Φ(x) is the standard Gaussian CDF
Weights each input x by the probability that a Gaussian random variable is less than x
Combines properties of dropout, zoneout, and ReLU: stochastic gating that is differentiable
Approximated efficiently as 0.5x(1 + tanh(sqrt(2/π)(x + 0.044715x³))) for fast computation

techniques.name: Label Smoothing
techniques.capability_it_enables: improved calibration and generalisation by preventing overconfident predictions
techniques.summary_verbatim: Label smoothing replaces labels with a smoothed version by mixing the hard labels with a uniform distribution to improve generalization and model calibration.
mechanism_atoms: Replaces one-hot target distribution y with smoothed targets: y_smooth = (1-ε)·y + ε/K where K is the number of classes
The model is trained with cross-entropy against these soft targets instead of hard one-hot labels
Reduces the maximum log-probability the model assigns to the correct class, preventing overconfidence
Introduced by Szegedy et al. (2016) in the context of Inception image classification

techniques.name: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
techniques.capability_it_enables: fine-tuning large models with 10,000× fewer trainable parameters
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks.
mechanism_atoms: Freezes all pre-trained weight matrices W₀ and adds a low-rank bypass: ΔW = BA where B ∈ R^(d×r), A ∈ R^(r×k), r << min(d,k)
Forward pass becomes h = W₀x + BAx; only A and B are trained
Matrices A initialised with random Gaussian, B initialised to zero so ΔW starts at zero
At inference, ΔW = BA can be merged into W₀ with no additional latency
Reduces trainable parameters by ~10,000× and GPU memory by ~3× compared to full fine-tuning

techniques.name: QLoRA
techniques.capability_it_enables: fine-tuning 65B-parameter models on a single 48GB GPU
techniques.summary_verbatim: We present QLoRA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.
mechanism_atoms: Quantises the frozen base model to 4-bit using a new NF4 (NormalFloat4) data type optimal for normally-distributed weights
Applies Double Quantisation: quantises the quantisation constants themselves to save additional memory
LoRA adapters are added on top of the 4-bit frozen model and trained in BFloat16
Gradients flow through the frozen 4-bit weights (dequantised on-the-fly) into the LoRA parameters
Uses paged optimisers to handle GPU memory spikes during gradient checkpointing

techniques.name: DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation)
techniques.capability_it_enables: enhanced LoRA fine-tuning by learning both magnitude and direction of weight updates
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) and introduce a novel weight decomposition analysis to investigate the inherent differences between FT and LoRA.
mechanism_atoms: Decomposes each pre-trained weight W = m · (W/||W||) into a magnitude scalar m and a unit-norm direction component
Keeps magnitude m and direction learnable; direction updates are parameterised via low-rank decomposition (LoRA)
At inference the directional low-rank increment is merged with the direction component before combining with magnitude
Achieves no additional inference latency compared to LoRA while consistently outperforming it on LLaMA and LLaVA benchmarks

techniques.name: Adapter Layers
techniques.capability_it_enables: multi-task NLP fine-tuning with only ~3.6% additional parameters per task
techniques.summary_verbatim: Adapter modules yield a compact and extensible model; they add only a few trainable parameters per task, and new tasks can be added without revisiting previous ones.
mechanism_atoms: Inserts small bottleneck adapter modules after each Transformer sub-layer (attention and FFN)
Each adapter is a two-layer feed-forward network: down-project to r dimensions, apply nonlinearity, up-project back
Residual connection around the adapter ensures near-identity initialisation
Only adapter parameters are trained; the backbone is frozen
Achieves within 0.4% of full fine-tuning on GLUE while adding only 3.6% parameters per task

techniques.name: Prefix Tuning
techniques.capability_it_enables: generation task adaptation using only 0.1% of model parameters
techniques.summary_verbatim: Prefix-tuning keeps language model parameters frozen, but optimizes a small continuous task-specific vector (called the prefix).
mechanism_atoms: Prepends a sequence of trainable continuous vectors (prefix tokens) to the key-value pairs of each Transformer layer
The prefix vectors are free parameters not tied to any vocabulary embedding
All actual model weights are frozen; only prefix parameters are optimised via backpropagation
At each layer, the prefix vectors participate in attention as virtual key-value pairs that the real tokens can attend to
Achieves comparable performance to full fine-tuning in high-data settings and outperforms it in low-data settings

techniques.name: BERT (Masked Language Modelling pretraining)
techniques.capability_it_enables: deep bidirectional contextual representations from unlabelled text
techniques.summary_verbatim: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.
mechanism_atoms: Randomly masks 15% of input tokens and trains the model to predict the original token from its left and right context
Joint conditioning on both left and right context in all layers produces deeply bidirectional representations
A second objective (Next Sentence Prediction) trains the model to predict whether two segments are consecutive
Pre-trained BERT is fine-tuned with a single task-specific output layer for downstream NLP tasks

techniques.name: RLHF / InstructGPT
techniques.subfield: alignment / reinforcement learning from human feedback
techniques.capability_it_enables: aligning LLM outputs with human intent across a wide range of instructions
techniques.summary_verbatim: We show an avenue for aligning language models with user intent on a wide range of tasks by fine-tuning with human feedback.
mechanism_atoms: Step 1: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on human-written demonstrations of desired behaviour
Step 2: Train a reward model (RM) on human pairwise rankings of model outputs
Step 3: Optimise the SFT model against the RM using Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO), with a KL penalty to prevent reward hacking
A 1.3B InstructGPT model is preferred by human evaluators over the untuned 175B GPT-3

techniques.name: SimCLR (Contrastive Learning)
techniques.capability_it_enables: learning high-quality visual representations without labels via contrastive objectives
techniques.summary_verbatim: This paper presents SimCLR: a simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations that simplifies recently proposed contrastive self-supervised learning algorithms without requiring specialized architectures or a memory bank.
mechanism_atoms: Generates two augmented views of each image using random crop, colour jitter, and Gaussian blur
Encodes both views with a shared encoder (ResNet) and a nonlinear projection head
Applies NT-Xent (normalised temperature-scaled cross entropy) loss to pull together positive pairs and push apart negatives
Projection head is discarded after training; the encoder representation is used for downstream tasks
Benefits from large batch sizes (4096+) as more negatives improve the contrastive signal

techniques.name: DINO (Self-Distillation with No Labels)
techniques.capability_it_enables: self-supervised ViT pretraining with emergent semantic segmentation properties
techniques.summary_verbatim: In the case of self-supervised ViT features, we also observe that the features explicitly contain the scene layout and, in particular, object boundaries.
mechanism_atoms: Uses a student-teacher framework where both networks share the same architecture (ViT)
Teacher network parameters are updated by exponential moving average (EMA) of student parameters, not by gradient descent
Student sees local/small crops; teacher sees global crops; cross-crop prediction objective forces multi-scale consistency
Teacher output distribution is sharpened (temperature < 1) and centred to prevent collapse
No negative pairs needed; collapse is prevented by centering and sharpening alone

techniques.name: Knowledge Distillation
techniques.capability_it_enables: compressing large ensemble or teacher model knowledge into a small deployable student
techniques.summary_verbatim: We show that it is possible to compress the knowledge in an ensemble into a single model which is much easier to deploy.
mechanism_atoms: Teacher produces soft probability distributions (soft targets) over classes by applying high-temperature softmax
Student is trained to match these soft targets via KL divergence (distillation loss) in addition to hard labels
Soft targets provide richer gradient signal than one-hot labels by encoding inter-class similarity structure
Temperature parameter T controls the softness: higher T spreads probability more evenly across classes

techniques.name: Quantisation-Aware Training (QAT)
techniques.capability_it_enables: integer-arithmetic-only inference with minimal accuracy loss
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a quantization scheme that allows inference to be carried out using integer-only arithmetic, which can be implemented more efficiently than floating point inference on commonly available integer-only hardware.
mechanism_atoms: Simulates quantisation noise during forward pass by fake-quantising weights and activations to integers then dequantising
Gradients flow through the quantisation operation using a straight-through estimator
Learns quantisation scale and zero-point parameters jointly with weights during training
Results in a model whose weights and activations can be stored as INT8 for deployment with no post-hoc calibration

techniques.name: Speculative Decoding
techniques.capability_it_enables: 2–3× faster autoregressive LLM decoding without changing output distribution
techniques.summary_verbatim: Speculative decoding is an algorithm to sample from autoregressive models faster without any changes to the outputs, by computing several tokens in parallel.
mechanism_atoms: A small, fast draft model autoregressively generates K candidate tokens in sequence
The large target model evaluates all K+1 tokens in a single parallel forward pass
A modified rejection sampling scheme accepts or rejects each draft token based on the ratio of target and draft probabilities
Accepted tokens are kept; the first rejected token is resampled from the target model distribution
Output distribution is mathematically identical to sampling from the target model alone

techniques.name: Gradient Checkpointing
techniques.capability_it_enables: training very deep networks with O(sqrt(N)) memory instead of O(N)
techniques.summary_verbatim: We design an algorithm that costs O(√n) memory to train an n-layer network, with only the computational cost of an extra forward pass per mini-batch.
mechanism_atoms: During the forward pass, only a selected subset of activations (checkpoints) are saved to memory
Non-saved intermediate activations are recomputed from the nearest checkpoint during backpropagation
Checkpoints are spaced approximately every sqrt(N) layers to minimise total memory under the sqrt(N) recomputation budget
In extreme cases, can reduce to O(log N) memory at O(N log N) compute cost
Reduces memory of 1000-layer ResNet from 48GB to 7GB with only ~30% additional runtime

techniques.name: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Stable on-policy RL training with large neural networks
techniques.summary_verbatim: We propose a new family of policy gradient methods for reinforcement learning, which alternate between sampling data through interaction with the environment, and optimizing a "surrogate" objective function using stochastic gradient ascent.
mechanism_atoms: Collects rollouts from current policy via environment interaction
Computes a clipped surrogate objective that limits the policy update ratio to [1-ε, 1+ε], preventing large policy shifts
Optimizes the clipped objective over multiple minibatch epochs per data collection phase
Includes a value function loss and an entropy bonus in the total loss to encourage exploration
Alternates data collection and gradient updates iteratively until convergence

techniques.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) — InstructGPT
techniques.capability_it_enables: Aligning language models to follow human instructions
techniques.summary_verbatim: We show that it is possible to significantly improve the ability of language models to follow a broad class of written instructions from humans, without sacrificing much performance on existing language modeling benchmarks.
mechanism_atoms: Step 1 — Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): fine-tune a pretrained LM on human-written demonstrations of desired behavior
Step 2 — Reward Model training: humans rank multiple model outputs; a reward model is trained via Bradley-Terry on these comparison pairs
Step 3 — PPO-based RL: the SFT model is further fine-tuned using PPO to maximize the reward model score, with a KL penalty against the SFT model to prevent collapse
The KL penalty coefficient controls how far the policy can drift from the supervised baseline
Evaluated via human rater preference judgements rather than automatic metrics

techniques.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
techniques.capability_it_enables: LM alignment from preference data without explicit reward model or RL
techniques.summary_verbatim: We introduce a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss.
mechanism_atoms: Derives a closed-form mapping from reward functions to optimal policies under a KL-constrained RLHF objective
Re-parameterizes the reward in terms of the language model policy itself, eliminating the need for a separate RM
Trains using a binary cross-entropy loss on preferred vs. rejected response pairs — the 'DPO loss'
No sampling from the LM during training is required, making training stable and lightweight
The implicit reward implicitly satisfies the Bradley-Terry preference model over paired comparisons

techniques.name: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Critic-free RL fine-tuning for LLM reasoning without a value network
techniques.summary_verbatim: GRPO eliminates the critic network entirely and instead samples multiple outputs for each prompt, using their group average as a proxy for the critic.
mechanism_atoms: For each prompt, samples a group of G outputs from the current policy
Computes advantages by normalizing rewards within the group: (r_i - mean(r)) / std(r)
Applies importance-sampling clipping (similar to PPO) using the group-normalized advantages
No value/critic network is needed — the group statistics replace value-function estimation
Used to train DeepSeek-R1 with verifiable binary rewards on math and code problems

techniques.name: InfoRM: Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
techniques.capability_it_enables: Detecting and mitigating reward hacking via information bottleneck
techniques.summary_verbatim: In this work, we tackle this problem from an information-theoretic perspective and propose a framework for reward modeling, namely InfoRM, by introducing a variational information bottleneck objective to filter out irrelevant information.
mechanism_atoms: Applies a variational Information Bottleneck (IB) to the reward model's encoder to compress representations to only preference-relevant information
The IB objective minimizes mutual information between input and latent while maximizing mutual information between latent and reward label
Overoptimization manifests as distributional shift detected as outliers in the IB latent space
Introduces the Cluster Separation Index (CSI) to quantify deviations in the IB latent space as an overoptimization indicator
CSI enables online mitigation strategies during RL training when overoptimization is detected

techniques.name: Uncertainty-aware Reward Model (URM / URME)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Quantifying aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in reward predictions
techniques.summary_verbatim: URM employs a probabilistic value head to capture aleatoric uncertainty by modeling the distribution of disentangled human preference attributes, while URME further quantifies epistemic uncertainty by examining discrepancies among individual URMs within the ensemble.
mechanism_atoms: URM replaces the scalar reward head with a probabilistic head that outputs a distribution over reward values
Aleatoric (irreducible) uncertainty is captured by modeling the spread of the predicted reward distribution
URME builds an ensemble of URMs; epistemic uncertainty is measured by the disagreement among ensemble members
Predictions with high uncertainty are flagged as unreliable and can be filtered or down-weighted during RL training
Evaluated on RewardBench, outperforming competitive large-scale baseline reward models

techniques.name: Probabilistic Uncertain Reward Model (PURM)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Learning reward distributions to delay onset of reward hacking
techniques.summary_verbatim: This paper proposes the Probabilistic Uncertain Reward Model (PURM), which generalizes the Bradley-Terry model to learn the reward distributions that emerged from the preference data.
mechanism_atoms: Uses a two-head neural architecture to output a reward distribution (not a scalar) for each prompt-response pair
Loss function derived theoretically as a generalization of the Bradley-Terry negative log-likelihood over distributions
Uncertainty per sample is quantified by the overlap area between the predicted reward distributions of preferred and rejected responses
High overlap indicates ambiguous preferences; low overlap indicates confident preference signal
Integrates an uncertainty-aware penalty into PPO to dynamically balance reward optimization against uncertainty-driven regularization

techniques.name: Reward Model Ensembles for Overoptimization Mitigation
techniques.capability_it_enables: Reducing reward hacking via ensemble-based conservative optimization
techniques.summary_verbatim: We conduct a systematic study to evaluate the efficacy of using ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives, specifically worst-case optimization (WCO) and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), for mitigating reward model overoptimization.
mechanism_atoms: Trains multiple independent reward models on the same preference data to form an ensemble
Worst-case optimization (WCO) optimizes against the minimum reward across ensemble members instead of the mean
Uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO) weights the optimization signal by ensemble agreement — penalizing regions of disagreement
Applied to both best-of-n sampling (BoN) and PPO-based RL fine-tuning
WCO/UWO practically eliminates overoptimization and improves performance by up to 70% for BoN in noisy label settings

techniques.name: Hidden-State Regularization for Generalizable Reward Models
techniques.capability_it_enables: Improving reward model OOD generalization via text-generation regularization
techniques.summary_verbatim: While previous research has advocated for constraining policy optimization, our study introduces a novel approach to enhance the reward model's generalization ability against distribution shifts by regularizing the hidden states.
mechanism_atoms: Retains the base LM's pretrained language modeling head alongside the newly added reward head
Incorporates a text-generation loss (next-token prediction) on the same hidden states used by the reward head
The generation loss acts as a regularizer that prevents the hidden states from collapsing to reward-specific spurious features
Both the reward head loss and the text-generation loss are jointly optimized during reward model fine-tuning
Markedly improves OOD reward accuracy and alleviates over-optimization in downstream RLHF

techniques.name: RewardUQ: Unified Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Reward Models
techniques.capability_it_enables: Systematic benchmarking of uncertainty quantification methods for reward models
techniques.summary_verbatim: This work introduces a unified framework, RewardUQ, to systematically evaluate uncertainty quantification for reward models.
mechanism_atoms: Provides a unified API to plug in different UQ methods (ensembles, Bayesian heads, conformal prediction) over reward models
Evaluates UQ methods along multiple axes: calibration, OOD detection, active learning efficiency, overoptimization mitigation
Tests epistemic uncertainty (from limited preference data) vs. aleatoric uncertainty (from inherent preference ambiguity)
Uncertainty-guided active learning reduces annotation cost by focusing labeling on uncertain samples
Serves as a baseline comparison framework for future uncertainty-aware RM research

techniques.name: Constrained RLHF for Reward Overoptimization
techniques.capability_it_enables: Preventing proxy reward overoptimization with constraint-based RL
techniques.summary_verbatim: Large language models are typically aligned with human preferences by optimizing reward models (RMs) fitted to human feedback, however, because any RM is only a proxy for human evaluation, this process is vulnerable to overoptimization, wherein past a certain point, accumulating higher reward is associated with worse human ratings.
mechanism_atoms: Models alignment as a constrained optimization problem: maximize primary reward subject to constraints on secondary reward models
Each component reward model is treated as a separate constraint with a threshold (proxy point) beyond which optimization is halted
Uses Lagrangian relaxation to convert the constrained problem to an unconstrained one with adaptive penalty weights
Constraint thresholds are set at empirically measured proxy points where further optimization hurts true human ratings
Evaluated under both best-of-n and PPO paradigms showing better Pareto tradeoffs than unconstrained baselines

techniques.name: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)
techniques.capability_it_enables: High-quality image synthesis via learned iterative denoising
techniques.summary_verbatim: We present high quality image synthesis results using diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models inspired by considerations from nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
mechanism_atoms: Forward process: gradually adds Gaussian noise to data over T steps following a fixed Markov chain schedule
Reverse process: a neural network (typically a U-Net) is trained to predict and remove the noise at each step
Training objective: a simplified reweighted version of the evidence lower bound (ELBO) that amounts to denoising score matching
Sampling: starting from pure Gaussian noise, applies the learned reverse transitions T times to produce a sample
Connection to score matching and Langevin dynamics enables theoretical understanding of training stability

techniques.name: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
techniques.capability_it_enables: Controllable conditional generation without a separate classifier
